name: PIVOT decision-preservation architecture
author: PIVOT project, adapted from OpenTikZ contributors
description: A detailed ICLR-style overview of PIVOT from candidate generation through adaptive-world evaluation, differential transfer, and evidence reporting.

parameters.name: \rowsep
parameters.meaning: reference vertical spacing between architecture layers

parameters.name: \boxminw
parameters.meaning: base width for process and external nodes

parameters.name: \boxminh
parameters.meaning: base height for process and external nodes

edit_contract.node_naming: fixed semantic nodes: generation (incumbent, operator, candidates, proxy), PIVOT (footprint, score, paired, correction, promote, decomposition), worlds (world0-world3), reports (metrics, evidence)

operations.summary: edit the corresponding label macro while preserving the node name
add a semantic node relative to an existing stage, connect it with an arrow, and include it in the appropriate fixed panel
switch a node between process, query, intervention, promotion, or world styles
adjust figurewidth or named spacing parameters for a venue column
change a W0-W3 world label while preserving the observer-to-strategic ladder
use only the named OpenTikZ palette colors and their tints/shades

invariants: the standalone document must compile without the paper preamble
the three fixed panels must remain behind all nodes and titles
semantic node names, world ladder, and feedback edge must remain intact
world0 must remain inside the adaptive-world panel
the feedback edge must remain inside the PIVOT panel boundary
world and reporting titles must remain inside their own panel boundaries
labels must not be placed on top of node text or other labels
colors must use only the five OpenTikZ palette names
